item: FX-G04 bursting charge of rifled shell and 6-pdr/mountain-howitzer shell
source: searched: same five books as VISFX-R03; the Confederate Ordnance Manual 1863 (Addenda p. 525-526) and the Field Manual 1862 (p. 19-21) describe the Parrott and Whitworth guns by dimensions only; the one burster figure for a rifled projectile is for the British Armstrong shell ('less than one ounce')

item: FX-G04 corroboration of case and shell bursting tables
source: The Field Manual for the Use of the Officers on Ordnance Duty, Ordnance Bureau, Richmond: Ritchie & Dunnavant, 1862; archive.org fieldmanualforus00conf; printed p. 76 (tables Charging Shells and Spherical Case Shot)
passage_ref: case: 6-pdr 38 balls 2.5 oz, 12-pdr 78 balls 4.5 oz, 24-pdr 175 balls 6 oz, 32-pdr 225 balls 8 oz; shell 'to burst' 11, 8, 5 oz for 32, 24, 12-pdr (burst row read from garbled OCR); service charge of the 12-pdr shell 7 oz (OCR, also in the 1864 Instruction p. 8-9)
notes: third printed source for numbers already used; added to TIERS.json basis. The prose on p. 23 of the same manual says 12-pdr case holds about 90 bullets and 1 oz of powder (agrees with the existing selectable scenario fa1863_ocr, contradicts the manual's own table); both stay carried, no default change.

item: FX-G03 Caledonia Furnace burning and location
verdict: burned June 26 1863 by Early's division; Franklin County, east of Fayetteville; off the loaded terrain
source: Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission marker 'Caledonia Furnace' (ExplorePAHistory marker 1-A-1DE, dedicated 1947), US 30 and PA 233, Caledonia State Park, Franklin County; fetched 2026-11-04
passage_ref: marker states furnace erected 1837 by Stevens and Paxton and destroyed by Gen. Jubal Early on June 26, 1863 (paraphrase, text not copied)
notes: secondary state-agency marker, so not 'documented'. OR reports of Early/Gordon/Ewell do not mention it (T1-005). Coordinates are not given by the PHMC page; crowd-sourced HMDB gives a point on a reconstructed furnace that may not be the original site, so no coordinate is adopted. The plan's 'about 2 miles out on the Cashtown road' is not supported by a Franklin County site. Furnace stays not drawn (off terrain).
